name: Phil Christopherson
residence: Gillette, Campbell County (moved there in 2014; 2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
occupation: Economic-development executive; he wrote that he was CEO of Energy Capital Economic Development in Gillette after earlier work in engineering, a computer-service business, teaching for the University of Wyoming Manufacturing Extension Partnership, and leading IDEA Inc. in Riverton (2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
education: Natrona County High School; degree in electrical engineering, University of Wyoming; M.B.A., University of Wyoming, 2006 (2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
prior_offices: Elected to the first city council of Covington, Washington (2024 WyoFile questionnaire); not a Wyoming legislative office
background: In his 2024 WyoFile questionnaire, Phil Christopherson wrote that he was born and raised in Casper, worked in his family’s trucking business, graduated from Natrona County High School, and earned a degree in electrical engineering from the University of Wyoming. He wrote that he would be 64 on Election Day 2024, married Lori Hauck in 1982, and that they have five children and 12 grandchildren. After UW he worked at Boeing in the Seattle area on AWACS avionics and later as a project manager; he also wrote that he served as a reserve police officer for the King County Police, helped form the city of Covington, and was elected to its first city council. He and his wife moved back to Wyoming in 1999.

He wrote that after returning he started a small computer-service business, taught lean manufacturing around the state for the University of Wyoming Manufacturing Extension Partnership, led IDEA Inc., Riverton’s economic-development group, and earned an M.B.A. from UW in 2006. The family moved to Gillette in 2014, where he was CEO of Energy Capital Economic Development; he wrote that in that role he helped start a business incubator and the Wyoming Innovation Center.
